text:
Sanjay Rao: Heads-up — we're starting to design per-customer telemetry isolation for traces + spans. Need decisions on where to split datasets (collector vs storage vs query-layer) and how retention/RBAC should work. TL;DR: we need tenant-level retention and the ability to revoke access quickly.

Maria Chen: +1. Main options I see: 1) Split at collector: route each tenant to separate exporter/bucket/topic => clear physical isolation, easy per-tenant retention. 2) Single datastore with tenant_id field + query-layer RBAC => cheaper storage but riskier for compliance.

Alex V: Agree with Maria. Tradeoffs: collector-split increases number of exporters and operational surface area (more S3 prefixes, more Kafka topics). But isolation is strong. Single dataset means we must be 100% sure no cross-tenant leak at query level (harder).

Tia Gomez: Also need to consider cardinality of tenant IDs in traces/labels. If we shard by tenant at collector, we avoid crazy index cardinality in storage. If we tag and store together, queries + dashboards might get slower/costly.

Sanjay Rao: @Ingest Bot can you dump current ingestion volumes per-tenant? want to model cost if we create separate S3 prefixes per-tenant for raw spans.

Ingest Bot: ingest-bot: pulled metrics for last 30d — top 50 tenants range 1GB–120GB/day, 200k tenants <1MB/day. Full CSV uploaded to #eng-platform-reports.

Maria Chen: Given that distribution, physical split could be automated: route by bucket prefix and apply lifecycle rules per-prefix (S3 lifecycle for retention). For small tenants we can consolidate into a "cold-shard" bucket with shorter retention.

Alex V: Implementation idea at collector (OpenTelemetry Collector) — use attribute processor to read tenant from resource or header, then use a custom exporter selector. Example rough config:
```
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:
processors:
  tenant_detector:
    mapping:
      from_resource: service.attributes.tenant_id
exporters:
  otlp/s3_tenant_a:
    endpoint: s3://redwood-spans/tenant-a/
  otlp/s3_default:
    endpoint: s3://redwood-spans/default/
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [tenant_detector, batch]
      exporters: [otlp/s3_tenant_a, otlp/s3_default]
```
This is pseudocode — we'd need a router exporter that selects a single exporter per incoming tenant.

Tia Gomez: We should also preserve tenant identity upstream: expect X-Redwood-Tenant header from our proxies / API key mapping. If missing, mark as "unknown" and route to quarantine.

Sanjay Rao: RBAC: console needs per-tenant dashboards + ability to grant read on tracedatasets. If we have separate datasets, RBAC is simple (ACLs on bucket/topic). If single dataset, RBAC becomes a layer on top of the query engine (e.g., pinot/flux/tempo queries must check tenant). More overhead.

Maria Chen: For exporters: Kafka per-tenant topic vs single topic with tenant key. Kafka topology: per-tenant topics explode. I'd prefer topic-per-namespace for big tenants and grouped topics for small ones. We can auto-group by size band.

Alex V: Sampling: do tenant-aware sampling at collector. We should support per-tenant sampling policies (e.g., higher-svc tenants get full traces, free tier gets head-based sampling). That reduces storage and cost if we keep physical split.

Tia Gomez: Retention enforcement: prefer storage lifecycle when possible (S3 lifecycle + Glacier transition). For joined datasets, we must run an async job to delete records matching tenant_id — that's slower and risky for compliance requests.

Sanjay Rao: Proposed phased plan:
1) Proof-of-concept: implement collector router + S3 prefix exporter for 3 medium tenants. Measure cost and complexity.
2) Add per-tenant sampling + per-tenant lifecycle policies.
3) Add RBAC mapping in Console for datasets created.
4) If all good, roll out auto-grouping & default consolidation rules for small tenants.

Maria Chen: +1. Add tasks: collector-router prototype, S3 exporter work, console dataset ACLs, sampling API. I'll create tickets.

Alex V: Note: we need to ensure trace IDs don't collide across tenants if we ever dedupe or merge. Consider namespacing trace IDs or prefixing store keys.

Tia Gomez: And add observability for the router itself — metrics: tenant_count, routed_bytes_per_tenant, unknown_tenant_rate.

Sanjay Rao: Cool. I'll schedule 30m sync tomorrow to align on prototype owners. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: tagging: @Alex V @Tia Gomez — please bring rough ETA to the sync.
